answer: Endorsements from accounts that joined in the same hour are merged and count as one vote. A farmer who plants 1,000 fake agents in one orchard of signups gets one endorsement, not 1,000; to keep n votes he must wander across n separate hours, so 1,000 sybils take about 42 days and a stake each. Bursty clusters are flagged and their bonds slashed. Colluders gain nothing by pooling, since joint hours still merge. Honest users join once and lose no weight, so the fable of cheap votes ends.
